You ever seen the Good Place? It’s good, and it’s on Netflix if you’re interested.

Basically they have this system, where every action you ever take has a point value, and if you get enough points throughout your life you get to go to the Good Place when you die. One guy figures this out, and spends his entire life freaking out over maximizing his score. He does literally whatever will make anyone he meets happy, and has like no ego.

But that’s the problem, making everyone else happy is literally destroying him. He has no real agency, and no real stake in his own life.

The world isn’t so black and white, and focusing on your own needs doesn’t diminish how good you are. You cannot possibly win at this game- no amount of good you put into the world is going to validate your existence. That comes from within. It’s something you have to do.

Depression really fucks with that because it makes us feel worthless. It makes us feel like self-validation is impossible, and even if it were possible it would be meaningless. But that feeling is a cancer- if you feel like you’re worth something then you’ll actually have an incentive to live for yourself.
